message.content: {"4": {"original": "Trackers can be legal targets as they assist in data distribution.", "rephrased": "Within the BitTorrent protocol, the servers that assist users in locating peers and downloading files are considered legal targets because they facilitate the distribution of data, even when the files themselves are not hosted centrally on these servers.", "summary": "BitTorrent trackers are legal targets for facilitating data distribution."}, "5": {"original": "Tracker administrators can easily remove torrents to stop downloads.", "rephrased": "Administrators of BitTorrent trackers possess the technical capacity to easily remove specific files from their systems, thereby effectively stopping users from downloading those particular torrents and mitigating the spread of unauthorized content.", "summary": "BitTorrent tracker administrators can easily remove files to stop downloads."}, "6": {"original": "eXeem was designed to be completely decentralised with no centralised trackers,但", "rephrased": "The eXeem file-sharing system was originally engineered to operate without any centralized tracking servers, relying instead on a decentralized network where every user's computer acted as a tracker to help others find peers, a design choice that distinguished it from centralized BitTorrent trackers before its development was halted due to the discovery of bundled adware.", "summary": "eXeem was a decentralized file-sharing system that ceased development after adware was found."}}
